result.summary: The image depicts a narrow residential intersection with sidewalks and a curb ramp featuring tactile paving. While the low-speed environment is conducive to safety, the lack of marked crosswalks and visual obstructions from parked vehicles near the corner increase risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A vehicle parked very close to the corner obstructs the sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection near the silver SUV

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The lack of painted crosswalks fails to designate a clear path for pedestrians or alert drivers to a crossing point.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Planters and a recycling bin on the sidewalk narrow the effective walking width for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk adjacent to the brick building

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and prevent vehicles from parking too close to the corner.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features basic infrastructure such as sidewalks and a marked crosswalk at a low-speed urban intersection. However, safety is compromised by parked vehicles obstructing sightlines and poor pavement quality.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corner and crosswalk significantly reduce visibility between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection, adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The roadway surface is heavily patched and uneven, creating potential tripping hazards for pedestrians crossing outside the marked area and affecting vehicle handling.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the foreground and center of the roadway.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and physically prevent parking too close to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Pavement Repair and Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the degraded road surface to provide a smooth, predictable path for all users.

result.summary: The street features a continuous sidewalk and mature trees, providing a basic level of pedestrian separation from traffic. However, the environment lacks formal crossing infrastructure, and parked vehicles along the curb create significant visual obstructions for anyone attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A line of parked vehicles along the curb blocks the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians who might step into the street.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the street safely.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement Surface
hazards.description: Large patches and uneven asphalt in the roadway could cause tripping or affect vehicle control.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is highly hostile, characterized by a complete lack of paved sidewalks, marked crossings, or traffic control infrastructure. Pedestrians are forced to navigate between parked vehicles and uneven, unmaintained dirt and broken concrete surfaces.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: The absence of dedicated pedestrian paths forces people to walk in the roadway or on unpaved surfaces.

hazards.name: Trip Hazards
hazards.description: Broken concrete and unpaved, weed-choked areas create significant trip hazards for anyone walking along the road edge.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals are provided at the intersection area, increasing exposure risk.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with curb ramps to provide designated and safer crossing points.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during low-light conditions.
